claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has high strength at room temperature and elevated temperatures, including around 1000 °C.
The proposed intervention is to substitute 5–10% of the HfMoTaTiZr composition with chromium during vacuum arc melting.
Chromium would replace a portion of the heavier refractory elements, although the elements and substitution ratios are not specified.
Chromium substitution will reduce the density of HfMoTaTiZr.
Adding 5–10% chromium will not significantly degrade room-temperature or approximately 1000 °C mechanical properties.
The chromium-modified alloy will retain a single-phase or near-single-phase structure.
Chromium addition may modify the alloy's lattice parameters.
The chromium-modified structure will retain cohesion and defect structures similar to those of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Chromium is a lower-density element than the heavier refractory elements it is intended to replace.
Replacing heavier elements with chromium will lower the alloy's average atomic mass and thereby lower its density.
Chromium can provide solid-solution strengthening in this alloy.
Chromium incorporation will retain or reinforce the solution-strengthening mechanisms of HfMoTaTiZr.
The chromium-modified alloy is predicted to have a density roughly 5–10% below that of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The modified alloy's yield strength and tensile strength are predicted to remain within ±10% of the as-cast alloy's values.
The predicted performance applies at room temperature and under thermal exposure up to approximately 1000 °C.
The predicted performance applies under high-stress mechanical loading typical of high-stress applications.
Chromium addition may produce secondary phases that weaken the alloy.
